newsitem.title: KENYA: FULL TEXT-Kenya central bank statement.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Kenya central bank statement.

text.p: The following is the full text of a statement issued by Central Bank of Kenya Governor Micah Cheserem on Wednesday:
"We are issuing this statement in the light of the developments in the foreign exchange market today.
The shilling exchange rate to the U.S. dollar opened at a mean rate of 64.00 shillings and rapidly depreciated to a selling rate as high as 69.00 shillings at 11 a.m. (0800 GMT).
While it was expected that the shilling would adjust downwards, following the lapse of the IMF loan, the speed of depreciation is causing concern.
Participants in the foreign exchange market should take note of the following factors:
1) The government has already committed itself to manage its expenditure within available resources.
2) Banks have reported that several importers are rushing to pay their foreign bills in order to minimise exchange losses.
3) Exporters, on the other hand, are reported to be holding back selling their foreign exchange earnings in anticipation of further shilling depreciation in order to make windfall gains.
4) Furthermore, it is being reported by commercial banks that some foreign investors in treasury bills and stocks are in the market to buy foreign exchange to repatriate their investments.
The combination of the above forces has caused the current turbulence in the foreign exchange market.
We are accordingly appealing to participants in the foreign exchange market to trade in an orderly manner so that losses arising from panic trading and speculative transactions are minimised.
The Central Bank wishes to reaffirm that it will continue to intervene in the foreign exchange market as and when justified."
